claim_contract.reproducibility_claim: the 64 retained rows establish bounded-summary fresh-instance reproducibility for the generated fixture and no stronger state-isolation or statistical-independence claim
claim_contract.pid_scope: categorical shared-exclusions MGW PID2 is the primary deterministic conformance decomposition. Categorical shared-exclusions MGW PID3 is exploratory and does not close pid-rs's separate 108-coordinate assurance program
claim_contract.numerical_scope: all 66 averaged informative, misinformative, and signed-net atom components, ten subset mutual informations, lattice identities, and one negative signed-atom theorem control are checked. The candidate wrapper receipts exact Rust output SHA-256 and byte size. Retained pointwise atoms are internally reconstructed but are not independently recomputed by the Decimal route
claim_contract.authority_boundary: the study is offline advisory research evidence. For fixed admitted authority input, Haldir authorization, trusted-state policy, and plant-command outputs are identical across PID record states. Audit records may vary. No operator-behavior noninterference is claimed

lenses.title: Claims and scope
lenses.defect_or_counterexample: Calling a physically parameterized synthetic fixture physical validation, or presenting a component implementation as field or deployment qualification, would outrun the evidence.
lenses.control_or_claim_removal: CLM-018 says synthetic categorical conformance, remains IMPLEMENTED, and enumerates forbidden physical, statistical, field, deployment, authority, and independent-review inferences.
lenses.remaining_risk: Readers may still generalize the drone vocabulary beyond the exact finite fixture. Publication must retain the limitations adjacent to the result.

lenses.title: First-principles semantics
lenses.defect_or_counterexample: Sources, target, row, ordering, units, or the relation between latent ENU coordinates and categorical symbols could be left implicit.
lenses.control_or_claim_removal: The fixture and typed question freeze ordered visual/radar/acoustic symbols, synchronized row windows, Boolean AND targets, natural-log units, the empirical law, and the pre-fusion dataflow boundary.
lenses.remaining_risk: This law is intentionally simple and cannot model unrepresented sensor noise, dropout, conflict, attack, or flight dynamics.

lenses.title: Mathematics and statistics
lenses.defect_or_counterexample: Repeated deterministic cells could be mistaken for an independent sample, negative atoms could be clamped, or MGW, I_min, KSG, continuous Ehrlich, BROJA, co-information, O-information, NIS, CUSUM, and correlation could be conflated.
lenses.control_or_claim_removal: The analysis declares an exact categorical empirical law with no confidence interval or p-value, preserves signed atoms, checks analytic PID2 identities and lattice reconstruction, and keeps each method in a distinct eligibility row with explicit abstentions.
lenses.remaining_risk: A finite-law numerical agreement does not establish estimator behavior on noisy, mixed, continuous, singular, or dependent operational data.

lenses.title: Type and state integrity
lenses.defect_or_counterexample: A swapped source, altered target, missing coordinate, non-finite number, stale source identity, or unbudgeted evaluator route could serialize a superficially plausible result.
lenses.control_or_claim_removal: Typed questions, exact source order, predicate-isolating mutations, finite-input checks, fixed coordinate cardinalities, source reconciliation, and explicit resource receipts fail closed.
lenses.remaining_risk: The retained fixture cannot demonstrate validity for source types or state combinations outside this closed categorical contract.

lenses.title: Time, ordering, and replay
lenses.defect_or_counterexample: Rows could mix windows, duplicate episode IDs, reorder source cells, or imply per-modality timing that the compact artifact does not retain.
lenses.control_or_claim_removal: The fixture validates one prior and observation timestamp rule, unique episode IDs, deterministic row ordering and digest, and a bounded row-window claim without asserting retained per-modality timestamps.
lenses.remaining_risk: The compact fixture is not a full producer replay and cannot expose hidden per-modality timing or lifecycle state.

lenses.title: Identity and provenance
lenses.defect_or_counterexample: The immutable producer preregistration, current evaluator revision, fixture bytes, schema bytes, and candidate build identity could be collapsed into one misleading version claim.
lenses.control_or_claim_removal: Separate identities bind the CREBAIN source commit, fixture digest, historical preregistered pid-rs revision, actual clean pid-core revision, evaluator adaptation, software identity, and schema digest.
lenses.remaining_risk: The final candidate output still needs a candidate-bound retained receipt. Source identity is not authenticity, scientific validity, or binary reproducibility.

lenses.title: Authentication and cryptography
lenses.defect_or_counterexample: A digest could be treated as producer authentication, or JSON normalization could detach an output from the bytes actually checked.
lenses.control_or_claim_removal: The release uses SHA-256 only for byte identity and custody, validates strict JSON and duplicate keys, and makes no cryptographic producer-authentication claim for the fixture.
lenses.remaining_risk: Repository and release signing establish separate source-publication provenance only after their own candidate workflow. They do not authenticate physical sensor truth.

lenses.title: Authority and safety
lenses.defect_or_counterexample: A downstream consumer could convert a favorable or unfavorable PID pattern into permission, denial, restriction, restoration, or a plant command.
lenses.control_or_claim_removal: The study output is record-only advisory evidence, the estimand graph has no authority edge, and CLM-018 explicitly forbids every grant, deny, restrict, restore, refresh, widen, revoke, and exercise interpretation.
lenses.remaining_risk: A future external consumer can violate this contract. Such a consumer requires separate admission, review, and evidence.

lenses.title: Hostile inputs and parsers
lenses.defect_or_counterexample: Duplicate keys, unknown fields, non-finite or oversized numbers, wrong cardinalities, malformed nesting, source swaps, or one-predicate mutations could evade a nominal happy-path test.
lenses.control_or_claim_removal: The schema checker is bounded and closed-world, its hostile suite isolates schema predicates, and Rust tests isolate scientific, identity, resource, order, target, and signed-component predicates.
lenses.remaining_risk: Candidate qualification must run the retained hostile suites. Static source review alone is not execution evidence.

lenses.title: Resource and denial-of-service bounds
lenses.defect_or_counterexample: A categorical route or JSON checker could allocate or compute before proving that dimensions, bytes, operations, and coordinates are bounded.
lenses.control_or_claim_removal: The fixed 64-row law uses explicit pid-core resource estimates and budgets for all nine calls. The schema checker bounds bytes, depth, numbers, arrays, and reference evaluation.
lenses.remaining_risk: These bounds cover this fixture and checker, not arbitrary larger studies or long-duration service availability.

lenses.title: Concurrency and lifecycle
lenses.defect_or_counterexample: Eight rows per cell could be advertised as proof that all hidden fusion state is isolated across initialization, cleanup, concurrency, restart, or crash boundaries.
lenses.control_or_claim_removal: The claim is narrowed to reproducibility of the retained bounded summary from producer-declared fresh instances. It explicitly denies complete state-isolation evidence.
lenses.remaining_risk: No complete state snapshot, concurrent producer campaign, crash-recovery trace, or long-running lifecycle evidence is retained.

lenses.title: Determinism and reproducibility
lenses.defect_or_counterexample: A result could be regenerated from mutable peer state, an unrecorded evaluator, a normalized fixture, or a different source order.
lenses.control_or_claim_removal: The source commits, fixture and schema digests, exact commands, source order, finite law, output schema, Decimal coordinate digest, and candidate gate are explicit and deterministic.
lenses.remaining_risk: Organizationally independent clean-room reproduction and cross-platform bit identity are not claimed.

lenses.title: API, FFI, and SemVer
lenses.defect_or_counterexample: A producer preregistered against an older pid-rs route could silently consume renamed, unbudgeted, experimental, or semantically different APIs.
lenses.control_or_claim_removal: The adaptation separates revisions, names stable budgeted categorical routes, checks package/source identity, freezes the estimand, and treats API review as a gate rather than inferred SemVer compatibility.
lenses.remaining_risk: Future pid-rs revisions require a new explicit adaptation and must not inherit this assurance by version string alone.

lenses.title: Schema, wire, and language parity
lenses.defect_or_counterexample: Rust serialization, prose tables, Python checking, and the declared public schema could accept different fields, atom orders, cardinalities, or semantics.
lenses.control_or_claim_removal: The actual Rust JSON carries an exact schema receipt, the external Python checker validates the public Draft 2020-12 schema bytes, and the Decimal route checks named and ordered coordinates from that same output.
lenses.remaining_risk: No third-party implementation or additional language binding is claimed to share these semantics.

lenses.title: Configuration and deployment
lenses.defect_or_counterexample: A user could treat canonical fixture thresholds, resources, source order, or method selection as a deployment-ready default profile.
lenses.control_or_claim_removal: All geometry, thresholds, resources, source order, and method eligibility are fixed study inputs. CLM-018 makes no deployment, ROS, network, credential, rollback, or operational acceptance claim.
lenses.remaining_risk: Real deployment requires separately preregistered targets, calibration, episode-level splitting, transport security, operational limits, and acceptance evidence.

lenses.title: Observability and forensics
lenses.defect_or_counterexample: A compact pass flag could hide the law, source identity, abstentions, resource use, method distinctions, negative coordinates, or errata.
lenses.control_or_claim_removal: The study emits typed fixture, schema, evaluator, errata, estimand-graph, method-eligibility, resource, atom-interpretation, algebra, and software-identity receipts with complete signed averaged coordinates.
lenses.remaining_risk: The fixture deliberately omits full producer execution state and full fusion output, so forensic conclusions remain bounded to retained fields.

lenses.title: Verification and evidence quality
lenses.defect_or_counterexample: One implementation could agree with itself, a schema pass could be mistaken for numerical validity, or a synthetic law could be called external validation.
lenses.control_or_claim_removal: Distinct gates cover Rust contracts, formal schema behavior, an 80-digit Decimal implementation that does not call pid-rs, actual-binary schema validation, and actual Rust-to-Decimal comparison. Each gate states its own boundary.
lenses.remaining_risk: The evidence is author-operated and repository-controlled. Independent human review, independent code, and representative field data remain absent.

lenses.title: Ecosystem composition
lenses.defect_or_counterexample: The fixture could be misconstrued as a live CREBAIN feedback edge, pid-rs authority, a Haldir decision route, or a Prisoma/ROS integration.
lenses.control_or_claim_removal: The ecosystem cut distinguishes immutable CREBAIN fixture source, optional pid-core evaluator dependency, offline Galadriel evidence, prospective record-only Haldir use, and absent Prisoma, ROS, command, and authority edges.
lenses.remaining_risk: Peer repositories can evolve. Only immutable pins and an exact candidate cut support this release claim.

lenses.title: Human factors and governance
lenses.defect_or_counterexample: Dense PID terminology, legacy fixture labels, or a rushed release could obscure method non-equivalence, negative atoms, limitations, or the lack of independent review.
lenses.control_or_claim_removal: Publication prose, equations, method matrix, typed errata, explicit limitations, exact commands, and this append-only assurance extension keep the bounded claim reviewable without rewriting historical tasks.
lenses.remaining_risk: Qualified independent human PID, statistical, security, and release review remains NOT RUN and must not be implied by machine-assisted review.

lenses.title: Counterfactual and unusual cases
lenses.defect_or_counterexample: A future patch could remove one target predicate, swap asymmetric source positions, clamp a negative atom, change one schema constraint, forge a clean-version label, or weaken CLM-018 while leaving nominal output plausible.
lenses.control_or_claim_removal: Predicate-isolating Rust and Python tests, asymmetric source/atom canaries, rotated targets, a fixed negative PID3 control, schema receipt binding, exact identity checks, and release-audit hostile claim mutations fail closed.
lenses.remaining_risk: Mutation coverage is bounded and cannot prove absence of every coupled defect. Exact-candidate execution and independent review remain necessary.

closure.residual_risk: The exact candidate must still run and retain every required gate. This finite synthetic conformance result cannot answer whether PID estimates are reliable, useful, calibrated, causal, or operationally beneficial on representative multi-sensor flight episodes.
